subject.title: Npm-valid package scopes with dots/underscores cannot map to ClawHub publishers

question: Should dotted and underscored npm scopes remain first-class ClawHub publisher identities under the exact scope-to-owner authorization rule?
rationale: This choice controls both public publisher identity and authorization to claim npm namespaces, so the shipped implementation cannot establish the permanent security and product contract by itself.

options.title: Ratify npm-compatible handles
options.body: Keep dots and underscores valid, preserve exact normalized scope matching, and document collision, reservation, URL, and transfer rules.

options.title: Introduce explicit aliases
options.body: Keep slug-safe public handles but design a reviewed scope-alias model that all publish, transfer, install, and UI paths understand.

options.title: Require package renames
options.body: Return to slug-only handles and require affected publishers to migrate their existing npm package identities.

recommendation.title: Ratify npm-compatible handles
recommendation.body: Keep dots and underscores valid, preserve exact normalized scope matching, and document collision, reservation, URL, and transfer rules.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the most complete ownership-policy analysis and are a repository collaborator positioned to route the decision.
